title: routing-rule-syntax-auditor-and-compatibility-shim
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: The current routing policy interpreter accepts a broad, hard-to-test DSL and several legacy fields that cause silent behavior changes when new rule shapes are introduced. This has resulted in routing surprises (wrong region selection under load), inconsistent fallback to cheaper model variants, and difficulty validating tenant policies during upgrades.

Goal: Implement a syntax auditor and a compatibility shim that validates routing config at ingestion time, warns on deprecated shapes, enforces a strict typed schema for new configs, and provides a runtime-compatible migration adapter for older rule shapes. The auditor should be pluggable so Dedicated/Private control planes can opt into stricter checks.

Scope:
- Build a standalone routing-rule syntax auditor that runs as part of the config API and CLI validator.
- Define a typed schema (JSON Schema + typed annotations) for the new canonical rule format covering region selection, tier routing, weights, and fallback model variants.
- Implement a compatibility shim that rewrites a subset of legacy rule shapes into canonical form at load time and flags non-rewriteable rules as errors or advisories depending on rollout policy.
- Add clear error/warning messages with remediation steps and links to a migration guide.
- Integrate with Console so PMs/Platform engineers see audit findings in the config history and rollout UI.

Out of scope: automatic live rewrites of rules in Dedicated clusters without operator approval, and attempting to canonicalize complex programmatic rules defined outside the standard DSL (these will be surfaced as manual migration work items).

Deliverables:
- schema definition file and unit tests
- auditor service + CLI hook + API integration
- compatibility shim library with opt-in strictness mode
- Console panel updates to show audit warnings/errors
- migration guide and quick-fix suggestions
acceptance_criteria: New canonical routing schema exists and is documented in Confluence with examples for region selection, tier routing, weighted fallbacks and deprecation mappings
Config API rejects invalid canonical rules with actionable error messages (HTTP 400) when strict mode is enabled
Compatibility shim automatically rewrites >=80% of legacy rule shapes used by current customers during test corpus run without changing semantics
Console surfaces audit warnings/errors in the policy details view and links to the migration guide
E2E tests cover ingestion -> audit -> runtime consistency for at least three representative topologies (multi-region, burstable-tier, fallback-to-variant)
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validator covering positive and negative cases
Integration tests: feed 200+ real-world rules from prod corpus to the auditor and compare outputs against expected canonical forms
Contract tests: ensure rewritten rules produce equivalent routing decisions in the policy simulator (latency and cost parity within 5%)
Console UI tests for warning/error display and links
Load test: validator throughput measured at peak rate (target 1000 writes/minute) with <200ms median validation latency
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): run auditor in logging-only mode against incoming configs for 2 weeks, collect analytics on rewrites and non-rewriteable rules
Phase 2 (opt-in strict): allow orgs to opt into strict validation; compatibility shim rewrites for these orgs applied automatically on save
Phase 3 (enforced): after 4 weeks and signoff, enable strict mode by default for new tenants and require migration for existing tenants with a 30-day remediation window
Rollback: provide an admin toggle to revert to permissive parsing and an export of affected rules for manual migration
implementation_notes: Use the existing policy transpiler as a baseline but move schema definitions to a centralized, versioned repo under /schemas/routing
Prefer JSON Schema draft-07 for broad tooling support and add typed annotations for enum/union discriminators
Auditor will be implemented as a small stateless service in Go (to align with config-api) with a library shim in the runtime (Rust) for parity checks
Compatibility shim rules should be logged with before/after diffs and a confidence tag for automated migration acceptance
Coordinate with Console team for UX copy — provide explicit 'why this failed' and 'how to fix' suggestions
